answer: The consequences of a successful password cracking attack can include unauthorized access to accounts, which may lead to data breaches, theft of sensitive information, and potential compromise of additional systems within a network. Once an adversary gains access to valid accounts, they can exploit this access for various malicious activities, such as data exfiltration, further infiltration into the victim's environment, or launching additional attacks [Source 2]. Additionally, successful password cracking can undermine trust in the security of the affected systems and lead to significant financial and reputational damage for the organization involved [Source 3].

## Attack description

An adversary tries every possible value for a password until they succeed. A brute force attack, if feasible computationally, will always be successful because it will essentially go through all possible passwords given the alphabet used (lower case letters, upper case letters, numbers, symbols, etc.) and the maximum length of the password.

## Execution flow

Brute forcing credentials may take place at various points during a breach. For example, adversaries may attempt to brute force access to [Valid Accounts](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078) within a victim environment leveraging knowledge gathered from other post-compromise behaviors such as [OS Credential Dumping](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003), [Account Discovery](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1087), or [Password Policy
